analysis.title: Innoviva Inc. (INVA): Broadly In-Line 3Q26 Financials
key_insights: INVA 3Q26 results were broadly in line with GS and FactSet consensus. Total revenue was $106.1mn vs GS $109.4mn and consensus median $112.2mn, down 1.6% y/y from $107.8mn in 3Q25.
Net royalty revenue was $54.7mn vs GS $52mn. Gross royalty revenue from GSK was $58.1mn. Net product sales were $49.4mn vs GS $54mn ($43.3mn US, $6.1mn ex-US).

EPS was a loss of $1.03 vs GS $0.50. The loss came mainly from a $139.5mn non-cash unfavorable change in fair value of equity and long-term investments, largely from a lower Armata Pharmaceuticals share price. Management says this does not reflect Armata's underlying fundamentals and remains confident in its prospects.
US net product sales were led by GIAPREZA ($23.1mn), XACDURO ($16.1mn) and XERAVA ($3.4mn). INVA continues to expect $150mn or more in IST US net product sales in 2026.
Income from operations was $42.2mn vs $34.6mn in 3Q25, up about 22% y/y.
GS is cautious on near-term royalties from GSK's Breo Ellipta and Anoro Ellipta. It sees rising headwinds as royalty loss of exclusivity approaches, with the IST business needing to drive growth.
INVA bought back 1,226,948 shares for $26.3mn in 3Q26 under its $125mn program. Since inception it has repurchased 3,829,116 shares for $82.7mn. Cash and cash equivalents were $581.4mn.
NUZOLVENCE (zoliflodacin) is now commercially available in the US. Management expects near-term revenue contribution to be very modest, with initial efforts focused on market access and distribution.

Updated guidance strengthens XACDURO's positioning as the preferred treatment for invasive carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) infections, which INVA believes supports broader adoption.
GS cut FY26 estimates: revenue $430mn from $441mn (-2.4%), EPS $1.04 from $2.56. FY27/FY28 EPS moved to $2.13/$2.29 from $2.10/$2.25.
GS keeps a Sell rating and a $18 12-month price target (unchanged), based on 8.0x applied to Q5-Q8 adjusted EPS. The stock closed at $21.26 on 4 Nov 2026, implying 15.3% downside.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Sell and $18 target on 8.0x Q5-Q8 adjusted EPS. It is cautious on GSK royalty trajectory as loss of exclusivity nears, and implied downside is 15.3% from $21.26.

earnings_insights: INVA 3Q26 reported total revenue $106.1mn vs GS est $109.4mn and FactSet consensus median $112.2mn (reported 11/5/2026 release).
INVA 3Q26 reported basic EPS -$1.03 vs GS est $0.50. The loss reflects a $139.5mn non-cash fair-value decline in equity and long-term investments, mainly Armata.
INVA 3Q26 reported net royalty revenue $54.7mn vs GS est $52mn. Net product sales were $49.4mn vs GS est $54mn.
INVA 3Q26 reported income from operations $42.2mn vs $34.6mn in 3Q25. Opex was $42mn vs GS est $39mn (SG&A $37mn vs $32mn, R&D $5mn vs $7mn).
GS estimates: FY26 revenue $430mn (old $441mn), FY26 EPS $1.04 (old $2.56), FY27 EPS $2.13 (old $2.10), FY28 EPS $2.29 (old $2.25). Quarterly EPS estimates: 4Q26E $0.52.
INVA expects $150mn or more in IST US net product sales in 2026 (company guidance).
risk_factors: Royalty revenue from Breo Ellipta and Anoro Ellipta faces rising headwinds as loss of exclusivity approaches.
Growth depends on the IST business, which must offset royalty declines.
Further fair-value losses on equity holdings such as Armata can hit reported EPS.

Upside risks to the Sell call: royalties declining less than GS expects, stronger critical care and infectious disease product ramps, higher value of strategic healthcare holdings, and acquisitions using INVA's investment capacity.
